narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: To lure young men into the army, 18th-century recruiters used wine, music, and this high-energy dance to demonstrate the physical prowess and noble status of military life.
This is Verbunk. 18th-19th century.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (TYgl6qfPdd4)
Title card: Verbunk · Hungary · 18th-19th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Verbunk developed alongside the verbunkos musical style between the mid-18th and early 19th centuries.
It originated from the 'verbuválás' practice, where the Habsburg army used music, dance, and drink to attract recruits.
It eventually became a symbol of Hungarian national culture during the 19th-century Romantic era.
on_screen: Map: Hungary · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a functional military recruitment tool, it evolved into a social dance used to open dance events.
It signifies masculine strength, freedom, and national pride.
In some traditions, it was performed upon request.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is characterized by energetic improvisation and a rich repertoire of motifs.
While usually an irregular solo form, some variants use a regulated circle or semicircle formation.
Key movements include rhythmic leg-slapping, heel clicks, and stamps.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Historically performed in village squares or taverns during recruitment drives.
Dancers often wore military-influenced attire or traditional peasant festive dress.
Today, it is performed at 'Táncház' (dance house) events and folklore festivals.

scenes.title: The people
narration: György Martin is cited as a prominent folklore expert who categorized the Verbunk within the 'new stratum' of Hungarian dance.
Researchers László Lajtha and Sándor Gönyey began systematic film documentation of the dance in the 1920s.
While widespread across the Hungarian language area, rare regulated variants in circles or semicircles exist.
The Verbunk is part of the 'new stratum' of Hungarian folk dance.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Verbunk (Hungary). New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.

wardrobe.policy: the narrator wears the dance's traditional apparel, reconstructed meticulously and respectfully from the sources
